task_retrieval_key: On March 7, 2018, a 35-year-old Chinese female presented with a one-year history of persistent erythematous papules and infiltrative plaques on the nose without any obvious triggers. Initially, a hard nodule the size of rice grains appeared on the right alar part of the nose, which was painless and itchy. Over time, the skin lesions gradually increased in size, became thick, and spread across the entire nose. Infiltrating plaques also developed on the upper jaw. Past and family history revealed no similar diseases within the family. Since the onset of the illness, the patient’s urine, stool, and weight remained normal. Skin examination revealed diffuse erythematous papules, infiltrations, and hypertrophic plaques on the entire nose and upper jaw, with a smooth surface.

avoid: Do not treat an unsupported agent assertion as clinical evidence
recommended_check: Verify source binding before using the evidence for support or refute
